problems.nature: phishing and credential harvesting via website impersonation
problems.description: Phishing attacks leveraging sophisticated HTML obfuscation and social engineering to impersonate legitimate websites, primarily targeting user credentials through fake login forms. Attackers exploit domain impersonation, malicious redirects, and embedded tracking pixels to evade detection and harvest sensitive information. These attacks often mimic well-known brands, use non-standard form action URLs, and override browser APIs to bypass automated defenses, posing significant challenges for detection systems.
attack_vectors: web-based phishing via fake login pages
social engineering through deceptive UI and content
credential harvesting via form submission to attacker-controlled endpoints
malicious redirects and tracking via embedded scripts and images

real_world_context.domain_insights: Attackers use hidden or obfuscated JavaScript to manipulate browser behavior and evade detection, embed fake login forms with suspicious action URLs, and employ domain names unrelated or obfuscated relative to the claimed brand. They embed tracking pixels and external legitimate resources to increase trustworthiness and complexity.
real_world_context.attack_sophistication: high - attackers employ advanced web techniques including API hooking, dynamic JavaScript obfuscation, multi-modal content manipulation, and social engineering localized in multiple languages to bypass traditional detection.
real_world_context.technical_implementation: Fake login pages contain forms posting credentials to non-official endpoints (e.g., 'free.php', 'process.php'), use JavaScript to override native APIs like navigator.geolocation, embed multiple hidden 1x1 pixel images for tracking, and load external scripts/stylesheets from legitimate domains to appear authentic.
real_world_context.threat_landscape: Phishing targeting major brands (Telekom, Instagram, Microsoft, Telegram) is prevalent, using free hosting platforms and complex URL structures embedding brand names in suspicious subdomains. These attacks are increasingly difficult to detect due to obfuscation and mimicry.
real_world_context.victim_impact: Users unknowingly disclose sensitive credentials leading to account compromise, identity theft, and potential financial loss. Organizations suffer brand damage and increased security incident response costs.

attack_signatures: phishing pages mimicking legitimate login portals with fake credential forms posting to non-official endpoints
JavaScript code that intercepts or fakes browser geolocation APIs to evade detection or fingerprinting
Use of hidden input fields and anti-automation techniques in login forms
Embedding of external stylesheets and scripts from legitimate domains to appear authentic
Use of social engineering text and brand names with mismatched URLs
indicators_of_compromise: form action URLs containing uncommon or suspicious filenames (e.g., 'free.php', 'process.php')
presence of multiple hidden 1x1 pixel images for tracking or data exfiltration
JavaScript functions overriding native browser APIs (e.g., navigator.geolocation)
URLs with excessive subdomain levels or unusual TLDs embedding brand names
HTML title and meta description mismatches with actual domain
detection_criteria: flag pages with form action URLs not matching the main domain or known trusted domains
detect JavaScript code that overrides or hooks native browser APIs
identify presence of hidden 1x1 pixel images used for tracking or data exfiltration
monitor for mismatch between page title/meta description and domain name
detect URLs with excessive subdomain levels or brand name obfuscation
normal_vs_malicious: legitimate login forms have action URLs matching the domain or trusted subdomains
absence of hidden or obfuscated JavaScript overriding browser APIs in benign pages
no hidden 1x1 pixel images used for tracking in legitimate sites
consistent use of HTTPS and valid SSL certificates in benign sites
URL structures with expected domain names and no excessive subdomains
measurable_thresholds: alert if form action URL domain differs from page domain by more than 1 level
flag if more than 2 hidden 1x1 pixel images are present
detect if JavaScript overrides native APIs with custom functions
consider URLs with more than 3 brand name tokens in subdomain as suspicious
trigger alerts for login forms with non-HTTPS or invalid SSL

attack_scenarios: A phishing page mimics the Telekom login portal but hosts the page on 'communityhomecare.org' with a login form posting credentials to 'free.php' on the same domain, embedding hidden 1x1 pixel images and JavaScript overriding geolocation APIs.

An Instagram-themed phishing site hosted on a free hosting platform uses a URL like 'instagram-verification-com-0fb9d4d5c638e553c69258afdd617c17.netlify.app' with multiple subdomains embedding brand names, includes social engineering text in multiple languages, and loads external scripts from legitimate domains to appear authentic.

A Telegram Web phishing page uses hidden input fields with encoded values and a form action URL 'process.php' to harvest credentials, while embedding tracking pixels and JavaScript that hooks browser APIs to evade automated detection.
legitimate_scenarios: A corporate login page with a form action URL pointing to 'login.corporate.com', consistent HTML title and meta description matching the domain, no hidden tracking pixels, and standard JavaScript without API overrides.
A banking website with HTTPS, valid SSL certificates, login forms posting to official subdomains, and external scripts/stylesheets loaded only from trusted domains with consistent branding.
An e-commerce site with standard navigation menus and footer links, user input fields with proper labels and accessibility features, and no suspicious or hidden scripts manipulating browser behavior.

risk_reduction: Implement strict URL validation ensuring form action URLs belong to the same domain or trusted subdomains.
Deploy DOM analysis and JavaScript behavior monitoring to detect API hooking and obfuscation.
Use content and metadata consistency checks to identify mismatches between page content and domain.
Apply detection rules to flag hidden 1x1 pixel images and suspicious form submission endpoints.
Continuously monitor URL structures and embedded external resources for trustworthiness using multi-modal analysis.

key_features_to_vary: form action URL domains and filenames
presence and count of hidden 1x1 pixel tracking images
JavaScript code complexity including API hooking and obfuscation
URL subdomain complexity and brand name embedding
social engineering text content and language localization
pattern_preservation: mismatch between page content branding and URL domain
use of suspicious or non-standard form action URLs
embedding of legitimate external scripts to increase trust
hidden input fields with encoded or suspicious data
realism_requirements: maintain realistic HTML DOM structure and text content volume
use plausible but suspicious URLs reflecting real-world phishing domains
include multi-modal features combining HTML and URL attributes
simulate typical user interaction elements like login forms and tracking pixels
reflect actual obfuscation and social engineering techniques observed
diversity_dimensions: vary attack sophistication from simple phishing forms to advanced API hooking
include different targeted brands and localized social engineering content
simulate multiple hosting platforms including free and paid domains
vary number and placement of tracking pixels and hidden inputs
alter URL complexity and domain obfuscation patterns
